stories.summary: The external debt of developing countries jumped at its fastest pace since the pandemic to a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, the World Bank said. Most of the increase was driven by private financing, with borrowing from private creditors and bond issuance by public enterprises rising nearly 35 percent. The poorest countries paid an average of 8.2 percent on new private loans — the highest since 1989 — and low- and middle-income countries paid $1.4 trillion in debt service, a fifth consecutive annual increase.
stories.why_it_matters: Record global debt and the cost of private borrowing are core development-economics exam facts.
